answer_1.quote: optimization in the long-context setting is now aimed at generating long outputs, typically in the form of extensive chain-of-thoughts (CoTs)...our study begins with a preliminary evaluation...examining whether popular base LLMs and their reasoning variants can effectively utilize information from lengthy inputs... Building on these findings, we propose a new framework for fine-tuning LLMs on challenging chain-of-thought data, termed Understanding-to-Reasoning Transition (URT) fine-tuning...reasoning in our approach involves generating the reasoning steps rather than merely interpreting them... We evaluate our URT fine-tuning method on several challenging reasoning benchmarks...
answer_1.outputs: long chain-of-thought responses (with intermediate reasoning steps and final answers)

answer_2.quote: We utilize three widely-recognized reasoning benchmarks to assess the problem-solving skills of our models: (1) AIME24 comprises 30 mathematical problems... (2) MATH500...is a curated subset of 500 competition-level problems. (3) GPQA Diamond...comprises 198 PhD-level STEM questions across Biology, Chemistry, and Physics...We also include MedQA..., LiveCodeBench-Medium..., BBH..., and Putnam-AXIOM...to evaluate our method across broader domains...

answer_4.quote: From the initial set of 180 generated solutions, we apply rejection sampling to eliminate 56 instances—those with incorrect answers (identified via rule-based matching) and those with correct answers but insufficient or flawed reasoning (determined through human review)... All the data are then subject to manual review to ensure that the reasoning steps are logically sound and free from overt mistakes...
answer_4.guideline: human review to determine sufficient reasoning quality and logical soundness
